title: Tonkotsu Ramen
description: A unique style of ramen consisting of an extremely rich, fatty pork broth.

ingredientGroups.title: Tonkotsu broth

ingredientGroups.title: Marinated Soft boiled Eggs

ingredientGroups.title: Chashu

steps.html: 1. Before any cooking, soak the bones in cold water in a large, non-reactive vessel, for at least 6 hours, and up to 24 hours. (I use a large plastic container).
2. The night before you want your broth ready, drain the bones, add them to a pot with fresh water covering them by 2 inches, and bring to a boil over high heat.
3. Drop the heat to medium, and blanch the bones, at a simmer, for 15-30 minutes, or until little to no scum rises.
4. Strain the bones again, and scrub away any black material, such as coagulated blood, from the bones and pot.

5. Return the bones to the pot. Add fresh water, and add in the fatback. If doing the night before, bring this to a boil, then down to the lowest setting on your stove, and cover. Then go to bed. If not, continue to step 7.
6. In the morning, bring the pot back up to a full boil, then back down to the lowest setting possible to maintain that jostling boil while covered. (For me, this is medium on my stove).

7. Depending on when you started cooking, continue to boil the broth for 12-18 hours, or until desired consistency and color is reached, meat has completely separated and broken down in the broth, and fatback pieces have mostly melted. Optionally, you can stir every 1-2 hours just to check up on things and promote more churning. Please feel free to add back water if the level gets too low.
8. Once cooked to your liking, strain the broth, discarding the solids, and reserve broth until needed over low heat. This broth keeps for around a week in the fridge.
9. If broth is not a creamy white, you can use a blender on high for 10 seconds to help with emulsion.

1. Combine the water, soy sauce, kombu, and niboshi in a sealed container.

3. Add the mixture to a small saucepan.

1. Add kansui powder and salt to the water, dissolve completely. If using both sodium carbonate and potassium carbonate, add them one at a time. Go slowly, stir constantly until clear. This will take a while, but eventually, the contents will dissolve. You can make the solution several days before to get a jumpstart, just hold the liquid in an airtight container.
2. In a standing mixer with a paddle attachment, add your flour and wheat gluten. Turn the mixer to “stir” and run for 30 seconds to aerate the mix.
3. While running the mixer on stir mode, add two thirds of your water mixture slowly in an even stream. Let the mixer stir the flour and water mixture for 5 minutes.
4. Add in the remaining water mixture with the mixer running, run for 2 minutes.
5. Turn off the mixer, and add the mixture to a sealable bag. Close, and let this rest for 2 hours at room temperature. Don’t skip this.

6. Knead it, by using an electric pasta machine to sheet the dough, going through the largest setting, then the 2nd, then the 3rd. Take the dough and fold it, sheeting under the 2nd widest setting, then fold it again and sheet it under the widest setting. Repeat this until the sheet is quite smooth and not ragged.
7. After kneading, put the dough back in the plastic bag, and rest at room temp for another 30 minutes.
8. Pull out your dough. Portion into workable sizes, and roll out to desired thickness with the pasta machine, using potato or cornstarch as you go to prevent sticking.
9. Cut your noodles to your desired thickness. 1.0 mm by 1.0 mm (setting 6) is around standard for these.
10. Bundle the noodles into 120 g portions and place them in a sealable bag. Put the bag in the fridge and allow it to rest for at least a day.

title: Pork Bao Buns
description: A homemade pork bao buns sweet and spicy.

ingredientGroups.title: Pork Belly
items: 2.2lbs pork belly sliced and chopped finger length

ingredientGroups.title: Toppings
items: 1 bunch of coriander or cilantro roughly torn
2 red chillies sliced into thin strips
4 green onions sliced into thin strips

instructionSections.title: Bao Buns, Braised Pork Belly & Glaze

steps.html: 1. Start by making the bao buns: place the flour, sugar, salt, and instant dried yeast in a bowl and mix together.

2. Add the milk, warm water, and softened butter to a jug and stir together until melted. Stir the liquid mixture into the flour mixture with a spoon and then by hand. Turn out onto a floured surface and knead for 10 minutes (or use a stand mixer fitted with a dough hook).
3. Place the dough in an oiled bowl, cover with clingfilm or a damp towel, and leave to prove until doubled in size (about 90 minutes to 2 hours).

4. Meanwhile, place all the slow-cooked pork belly ingredients (not the glaze) into a cast-iron casserole pan. Bring to a boil, cover with a lid, turn down the heat, and simmer for 2 hours. Turn off the heat and drain the pork (reserve the flavorful stock for noodle soup if desired).
5. Tip the proved dough onto a floured surface, knead briefly, and divide into balls. Roll each ball into an oval on baking parchment (approx. 12cm x 8cm).
6. Brush the ovals lightly with olive oil and fold each oval over a chopstick in the middle to leave a little space in the fold, then slide out the chopstick.
7. Transfer the folded buns (still on their parchment squares) onto baking trays, cover loosely, and prove for 1 more hour until puffed up.
8. Bring a large steamer pan to a boil. Steam the buns in batches on their parchment squares for 15 minutes until pillowy and cooked through.
9. Chop the braised pork belly into bite-sized chunks and whisk together the glaze ingredients in a small bowl.
10. Heat vegetable oil in a frying pan over high heat. Fry the pork with a pinch of salt and pepper until golden, then pour in the glaze and cook for 6-7 minutes until dark, glossy, and sticky.
11. Open the warm steamed buns and stuff generously with sticky pork belly, fresh torn cilantro, sliced red chillies, spring onion strips, sesame seeds, and chopped toasted cashews.

title: Chicken Tikka Masala with Naan Bread
description: A traditional Indian dish made up of chicken that's been marinated in yogurt, served with rice.

ingredientGroups.title: Chicken Marinade
items: 28 oz (1.75 lbs / 800g) boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
1 teaspoon Kashmiri chili (or 1/2 teaspoon ground red chili powder)

ingredientGroups.title: Naan
items: 1 (.25 ounce) package active dry yeast (about 2 1/4 teaspoons)
3 1/2 cups all-purpose flour (or 2 cups white whole wheat flour + 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour)

ingredientGroups.title: Sauce
items: 2 small onions (or 1 large onion) finely diced
1 teaspoon Kashmiri chili (optional for colour and flavour)
1/2 teaspoon ground red chili powder (adjust to your taste preference)
1 1/4 cups of heavy or thickened cream (use evaporated milk for lower calories)
4 tablespoons Fresh cilantro or coriander to garnish

steps.html: 1. In a bowl, combine chicken with all of the ingredients for the chicken marinade; let marinate for 10 minutes to an hour (or overnight if time allows).

2. Heat oil in a large skillet or pot over medium-high heat. When sizzling, add chicken pieces in batches of two or three, making sure not to crowd the pan. Fry until browned for only 3 minutes on each side. Set aside and keep warm. (You will finish cooking the chicken in the sauce.)
3. Melt the butter in the same pan. Fry the onions until soft (about 3 minutes) while scraping up any browned bits stuck on the bottom of the pan.
4. Add garlic and ginger and sauté for 1 minute until fragrant, then add garam masala, cumin, turmeric and coriander. Fry for about 20 seconds until fragrant, while stirring occasionally.
5. Pour in the tomato puree, chili powders and salt. Let simmer for about 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally until sauce thickens and becomes a deep brown red colour.

6. Stir the cream and sugar through the sauce. Add the chicken and its juices back into the pan and cook for an additional 8-10 minutes until chicken is cooked through and the sauce is thick and bubbling. Pour in the water to thin out the sauce, if needed.
7. Garnish with cilantro (coriander) and serve with hot garlic butter rice and fresh homemade Naan bread!
1. Stir together warm water and honey until the honey has dissolved.

2. Add the water mixture to the bowl of a stand mixer with the dough attachment, and sprinkle the yeast on top of the water. Give the yeast a quick stir to mix it in with the water. Then let it sit for 5-10 minute until the yeast is foamy.

3. Turn the mixer onto low speed, and add gradually flour, yogurt, salt, baking powder, and egg. Increase speed to medium-low, and continue mixing the dough for 2-3 minutes, or until the dough is smooth. (The dough will still be slightly sticky, but should form into a ball that pulls away from the sides of the mixing bowl.)

4. Remove dough from the mixing bowl, and use your hands to shape it into a ball. Grease the mixing bowl (or a separate bowl) with olive oil or cooking spray, then place the dough ball back in the bowl and cover it with a damp towel. Place in a warm location (I set mine by the sunny window) and let it rise for 1 hour until the dough has nearly doubled in size.

5. Meanwhile, heat the butter in a small saute pan over medium heat until melted. Add garlic and cook for 1-2 minutes until fragrant. Then remove butter from heat, strain out and discard the garlic, leaving the infused melted butter behind. Set aside.

6. Once the dough is ready, transfer it to a floured work surface. Then cut the dough into 8 separate pieces. Roll each into a ball with your hands, then place on the floured surface and use a rolling pin to roll out the dough into a large circle (or oval, or whatever shape it takes) until the dough is a little less than 1/4-inch thick. Brush dough lightly with the garlic-infused butter on both sides.

7. Heat a large cast-iron skillet or heavy saute pan over medium-high heat. Add a piece of the rolled-out dough to the pan and cook for 1 minute, or until the dough begins to bubble and the bottom turns lightly golden. Flip the dough and cook on the second side for 30-60 seconds, or until the bottom is golden. Then transfer the naan to a separate plate, and cover with a towel. Repeat with remaining dough until all of the naan pieces are cooked.
8. Keep the naan covered with the towel until ready to serve, so that it doesn’t dry out. Serve sprinkled with fresh cilantro, if desired.

title: Birria Quesa Tacos
description: Tortillas filled with the stew's tender, juicy meat dipped in meat broth.

ingredientGroups.title: Quesatacos
items: 6 inch corn tortillas (a large pack will do)

steps.html: 1. Start by removing the stems and seeds of ancho and guajilo chilies, as well as chilies de arbol.

2. Season all the meat generously with salt. In a large oiled pot heated over medium heat, add the meat in batches and sear 2-3 minutes on all sides. Once seared, take out the meat and leave on the side.
3. Add a bit more oil to the pot back on medium heat and add chopped onions. Saute until just softened.
4. Once softened, add tomato paste and cook down until paste starts to darken.
5. At which point, add sliced garlic and saute until fragrant and add rich beef stock. Mix together and add in chilies.
6. Add the meat back in.
7. Separately in cheesecloth, add black pepper corns, toasted coriander, cinnamon stick, and bay leaves. Fold together and tie tightly.
8. Toss the spice bag mixture into the stock and bring to a light simmer and cover. Braise for 1 hour stirring occasionally.
9. After 1 hour, remove the chilies and place into a blender with a little of stock liquid and blend until smooth.
10. Pour back into the stew and bring back to a simmer. Cover and braise for 90 minutes.
11. Remove the meat (and any bones) and shred using a fork.
12. Season the rest of the broth with salt and place to the side.
1. Take a fresh tortilla and dunk in the broth completely.
2. Place tortilla in a cast iron skillet set over medium heat.
3. Top with shredded cheese (preferably oaxaca cheese) and cook until just melted.
4. On one side add the braised shredded meat with a drizzle of consomme.
5. Fold the taco over cooking for 1-2 minutes. Flip and cook for another 1-2 minutes.
6. Serve with a ramekin filled with consomme topped with diced onions and chopped cilantro.

title: Ash Reshteh
description: A classic Persian noodle soup with beans and herbs that is intensely aromatic and amazingly delicious

items: 1/4 cup dried white beans, such as navy or cannellini
Fine sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
6 tablespoons plus 1/3 cup extra-virgin olive oil
2 large yellow onions, 1 finely chopped and 1 thinly sliced
1 cup dried green or brown lentils
2 quarts chicken or beef stock (preferably homemade), or water
1 1/2 cups liquid kashk (Persian sun-dried yogurt or whey), plus 1/2 cup, for serving

steps.html: 1. The night before you plan to cook, place chickpeas and white beans in a medium bowl. Add a generous pinch of salt and 2 cups water. Refrigerate overnight.

2. The night before or just before cooking, prepare the herbs and greens: Wash spinach, cilantro and parsley, then use a salad spinner to dry very well. Run a knife through the spinach to cut leaves into large pieces. Trim the woody ends from cilantro, parsley and dill so that only leaves and tender stems remain. Roughly chop cilantro, parsley, dill, chives and mint leaves into pieces no larger than a quarter. If preparing ahead of time, wrap chopped greens and herbs in plastic bags and refrigerate overnight.

3. To cook, set a large (at least 10-quart) Dutch oven or stockpot over medium heat and add 4 tablespoons oil. When the oil shimmers, add the chopped onion and a generous pinch of salt. Cook, stirring regularly, until the onion is tender and golden brown, 16 to 18 minutes. Add garlic and cook, stirring constantly, for 1 minute.

4. Drain the beans and add to onion along with the lentils, turmeric and 1 teaspoon pepper. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring to coat the beans with oil and spices. Add the chopped spinach and herbs, along with stock or water, and stir to combine. Partly cover the pot with a lid and bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to simmer the soup for 1 hour, stirring regularly to prevent the greens from sticking and burning. If the soup remains very thick even after the greens have wilted, add another 1 to 2 cups water, as needed to thin it.

5. Place 1 1/2 cups kashk in a medium bowl. Add a ladle or two of hot soup and whisk to dissolve, then add the mixture to the pot. The kashk will change the color of the soup from bright to milky green. Increase the heat and bring the soup to a boil, then break the noodles in half and add to the pot. Stir gently to mix in the noodles and keep them from sticking together, then reduce heat and simmer, stirring occasionally, until noodles are soft and chewy and the beans are completely tender, about 30 minutes.

1. In the meantime, prepare the garnishes: Set a medium frying pan over medium-high heat. When the pan is hot, add 2 tablespoons oil. When the oil shimmers, add sliced onion and a generous pinch of salt. Cook, stirring regularly, until golden brown and caramelized, 16 to 18 minutes. Spread cooked onion onto a paper towel-lined plate to absorb excess oil; let cool. Wipe out pan and return to medium heat. Add remaining 1/3 cup oil and warm gently over low heat, then stir in dried mint and remove from heat. Set mint oil aside and allow to steep for at least 5 minutes.
2. Place remaining 1/2 cup kashk in a small bowl and thin out with a few tablespoons of water until it’s the texture of thin yogurt. Set aside.

3. The soup should be as thick as a hearty chili. If it’s any thicker, thin it with water, 1/2 cup at a time. Taste and adjust the seasoning with salt as needed, accounting for the fact that both the noodles and the kashk are well salted.
4. To serve, ladle soup into individual bowls. Drizzle with reserved kashk and mint oil, then top with a sprinkling of golden onions.

description: A bakery product that contains dough/roll-in fat layers to create a flaky, crispy texture

ingredientGroups.title: FOR THE DÉTREMPE (DOUGH)
items: 4 ⅔ cups/605 grams all-purpose or bread flour, plus more for dustingd
1 tablespoon plus 1/2 teaspoon/12 grams kosher saltd
3/4cup plus 2 tablespoons/214 grams water, at room temperatured
1/2 cup/120 grams whole milk, at room temperatured
1/4 cup/57 grams unsalted butter, cut into 1/2-inch pieces, chilled

ingredientGroups.title: FOR THE BUTTER BLOCK AND ASSEMBLY
items: 1 1/2 cups/340 grams unsalted European or European-style butter (3 sticks), chilled

steps.html: 1. Twenty-four hours before serving, start the détrempe: In the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the dough hook, combine the flour, sugar, salt and yeast, and stir to combine. Create a well in the center, and pour in the water and milk. Mix on low speed until a tight, smooth dough comes together around the hook, about 5 minutes. Remove the hook and cover the bowl with a damp towel. Set aside for 10 minutes.

2. Reattach the dough hook and turn the mixer on medium-low speed. Add the butter pieces all at once and continue to mix, scraping down the bowl and hook once or twice, until the dough has formed a very smooth, stretchy ball that is not the least bit sticky, 8 to 10 minutes.

3. Form the dough into a ball and place seam-side down on a lightly floured work surface. Using a sharp knife, cut two deep perpendicular slashes in the dough, forming a “+.” (This will help the dough expand into a square shape as it rises, making it easier to roll out later.) Place the dough slashed-side up inside the same mixing bowl, cover with plastic wrap and let rise at room temperature until about 1 1/2 times its original size, 45 minutes to 1 hour. Transfer the bowl to the refrigerator and chill for at least 4 hours and up to 12.

1. As the dough chills, make the butter block: Place the sticks of butter side-by-side in the center of a large sheet of parchment paper, then loosely fold all four sides of the parchment over the butter to form a packet. Turn the packet over and use a rolling pin to lightly beat the cold butter into a flat scant 1/2-inch-thick layer, fusing the sticks and making it pliable. (Don’t worry about the shape at this point.) The parchment may tear. Turn over the packet and unwrap, replacing the parchment with a new sheet if needed. Fold the parchment paper over the butter again, this time making neat, clean folds at right angles (like you’re wrapping a present), forming an 8-inch square. Turn the packet over again and roll the pin across the packet, further flattening the butter into a thin layer that fills the entire packet while forcing out any air pockets. The goal is a level and straight-edged square of butter. Transfer the butter block to the refrigerator.

2. Eighteen hours before serving, remove the dough from the refrigerator, uncover and transfer to a clean work surface. (It will have doubled in size.) Deflate the dough with the heel of your hand. Using the four points that formed where you slashed the dough, stretch the dough outward and flatten into a rough square measuring no more than 8 inches on one side.

3. Place 2 pieces of plastic wrap on the work surface perpendicular to each other, and place the dough on top. Wrap the dough rectangle, maintaining the squared-off edges, then roll your pin over top as you did for the butter, forcing the dough to fill in the plastic and form an 8-inch square with straight sides and right angles. Freeze for 20 minutes.

4. Remove the butter from the refrigerator and the dough from the freezer. Set aside the butter. Unwrap the dough (save the plastic, as you’ll use it again) and place on a lightly floured surface. Roll the dough, dusting with flour if necessary, until 16 inches long, maintaining a width of 8 inches (barely wider than the butter block). With a pastry brush, brush off any flour from the surface of the dough and make sure none sticks to the surface.

5. You’re going to enclose the butter block in the dough and roll them out together. To ensure they do so evenly, they should have the same firmness, with the dough being slightly colder than the butter. The butter should be chilled but able to bend without breaking. If it feels stiff or brittle, let sit at room temperature for a few minutes. Unwrap the butter just so the top is exposed, then use the parchment paper to carefully invert the block in the center of the dough rectangle, ensuring all sides are parallel. Press the butter gently into the dough and peel off the parchment paper. You should have a block of butter with overhanging dough on two opposite sides and a thin border of dough along the other two.

6. Grasp the overhanging dough on one side and bring it over the butter toward the center, then repeat with the other side of the dough, enclosing the butter. You don’t need the dough to overlap, but you want the two sides to meet, so stretch it if necessary, and pinch the dough together along all seams so no butter peeks out anywhere. Lift the whole block and dust a bit of flour underneath, then rotate the dough 90 degrees, so the center seam is oriented vertically.

7. Orient the rolling pin perpendicular to the seam and lightly beat the dough all along the surface to lengthen and flatten. Roll out the dough lengthwise along the seam into a 24-inch-long, 1/4-inch-thick narrow slab, lightly dusting underneath and over top with more flour as needed to prevent sticking. Rather than applying pressure downward, try to push the dough toward and away from you with the pin, which will help maintain even layers of dough and butter. Remember to periodically lift the dough and make sure it’s not sticking to the surface, and try your best to maintain straight, parallel sides. (It’s OK if the shorter sides round a bit, you’re going to trim them.)

8. Use a wheel cutter or long, sharp knife to trim the shorter ends, removing excess dough where the butter doesn’t fully extend and squaring off the corners for a very straight-edged, even rectangle of dough. Maintaining the rectangular shape, especially at this stage, will lead to the most consistent and even lamination. If at any point in the process you see air bubbles in the dough while rolling, pierce them with a cake tester or the tip of a paring knife to deflate and proceed.

9. Dust any flour off the dough’s surface. Grasp the short side of the rectangle farther from you and fold it toward the midline of the dough slab, aligning the sides. Press gently so the dough adheres to itself. Repeat with the other side of the dough, leaving an 1/8-inch gap where the ends meet in the middle. Now, fold the entire slab in half crosswise along the gap in the center. You should now have a rectangular packet of dough, called a “book,” that’s four layers thick. This is a “double turn,” and it has now quadrupled the number of layers of butter inside the dough.

10. Wrap the book tightly in the reserved plastic. If it is thicker than about 1 1/2 inches, or if it’s lost some of its rectangularity, roll over the plastic-wrapped dough to flatten it and reshape it. Freeze the book for 15 minutes, then refrigerate for 1 hour.

11. Let the dough sit at room temperature for about 5 minutes. Unwrap and place on a lightly floured surface. Beat the dough and roll out as before (Step 10) into another long, narrow 3/8-inch-thick slab. It should be nice and relaxed, and extend easily. Dust off any excess flour.

12. Fold the dough in thirds like a letter, bringing the top third of the slab down and over the center third, then the bottom third up and over. This is a “simple turn,” tripling the layers. Press gently so the layers adhere. Wrap tightly in plastic again and freeze for 15 minutes, then refrigerate for 1 hour.

13. Let the dough sit at room temperature for about 5 minutes, then unwrap and place on a lightly floured surface. Beat the dough and roll out as before, but into a 14-by-17-inch slab (15-by-16-inch for pain au chocolat or ham and cheese croissants). The dough will start to spring back, but try to get it as close to those dimensions as possible. Brush off any excess flour, wrap tightly in plastic, and slide onto a baking sheet or cutting board. Freeze for 20 minutes, then chill overnight (8 to 12 hours). If making pain au chocolat or ham and cheese croissants, see recipes.

14. Four and a half hours before serving, arrange racks in the upper and lower thirds of the oven. Bring a skillet of water to a simmer over medium-high heat. Transfer the skillet to the floor of the oven and close the door. (The steam released inside the oven will create an ideal proofing environment.)

15. As the steam releases in the oven, line two rimmed baking sheets with parchment paper and set aside. Let the dough sit at room temperature for about 5 minutes. Unwrap (save the plastic for proofing), place on a very lightly floured surface, and, if necessary, roll out to 17-by-14 inches. Very thoroughly dust off any excess flour with a pastry brush. Use a wheel cutter or long knife and ruler to cut the shorter sides, trimming any irregular edges where not all the layers of dough fully extend and creating a rectangle that’s exactly 16 inches long, then cut into four 4-by-14-inch rectangles.

16. Separate the rectangles, then use the ruler and wheel cutter to slice a straight line from opposite corners of one rectangle to form two long, equal triangles. Repeat with the remaining rectangles to make 8 triangles. Trim the short side of each triangle at a slight angle, making them into triangles with longer sides of equal length.

17. Working one triangle at a time, grasp the two corners of the shorter end, the base of the crescent, and tug gently outward to extend the points and widen the base to about 3 inches. Then, gently tug outward from about halfway down the triangle all the way to the point, to both lengthen the triangle and thin the dough as it narrows. Starting at the base (the short end), snugly roll up the dough, keeping the point centered and applying light pressure. Try not to roll tightly or stretch the dough around itself. Place the crescent on one of the parchment-lined baking sheets, resting it on the point of the triangle. If the dough gets too soft while you’re working, cover the triangles and freeze for a few minutes before resuming rolling. Space them evenly on the baking sheets, four per sheet. Very loosely cover the baking sheets with plastic wrap, so the croissants have some room to expand.

18. Three and a half hours before serving, open the oven and stick your hand inside: It should be humid but not hot, as the water in the skillet will have cooled. You want the croissants to proof at 70 to 75 degrees. (Any hotter and the butter will start to melt, leading to a denser croissant.) Place the baking sheets inside the oven and let the croissants proof until they’re about doubled in size, extremely puffy, and jiggle delicately when the baking sheet is gently shaken, 2 to 2 1/2 hours. Resist the urge to touch or poke the croissants as they proof: They’re very delicate. Try not to rush this process, either, as an underproofed croissant will not be as light and ethereal.

19. Remove the baking sheets from the oven and carefully uncover them, then transfer to the refrigerator and chill for 20 minutes while you heat the oven. Remove the skillet from the oven and heat to 375 degrees.

20. In a small bowl, stir the yolk and heavy cream until streak-free. Using a pastry brush, gently brush the smooth surfaces of each crescent with the yolk and cream mixture, doing your best to avoid the cut sides with exposed layers of dough.

21. Transfer the sheets to the oven and bake for 20 minutes. Rotate the baking sheets and switch racks, and continue to bake until the croissants are deeply browned, another 10 to 15 minutes. Remove from the oven and let cool completely on the baking sheets.

2. Once thick, remove from heat and let it cool to room temperature.

3. In a stand mixer bowl, add the dry ingredients. Add in milk and yeast mixture, the tangzhong mix, and a whole egg. Mix on low speed, scraping the sides occasionally. When dough starts coming together, increase speed to medium-low. Gradually add butter until incorporated and nothing sticks to the sides. About 5-7 minutes.

4.Dump dough onto a work surface and roll into a tight ball. Place dough into a lightly greased bowl and cover with a damp towel or plastic wrap. Let rise at room temperature for 1-2 hours, or doubled in size.

5.Roll out the dough into an oval shape. Flip it over so the surface (crust) is on the bottom. Letter fold: Fold the top and bottom third over the center. Rotate 90° and roll it up to form a spiral while pressing down. Pinch the seam closed and add three pieces seam side down into a loaf pan. Proof in a warm, humid place until it doubles in size or it's 1cm below the rim of the loaf pan (1-2hours)
6. Preheat oven to 350 F and bake for 30 minutes or until internal temp is 190 F

title: Reverse-Sear Prime Rib Roast
description: 48-hour rosemary-umami dry-brined bone-in prime rib roasted low-and-slow for edge-to-edge medium-rare, served with silky melted onions, horseradish cream, and red wine au jus.

ingredientGroups.title: The Roast & Seasoning
items: 1 (6 to 7.6 lb) bone-in prime rib roast (3 ribs), cut and tied by butcher
2.5 to 3 tbsp Rosemary Salt (from batch below; up to 1/3 cup for 7.6 lb roast)
1/2 tsp MSG (or 1 tbsp finely ground dried porcini mushroom powder)
2 tbsp neutral high-heat oil (avocado or grapeseed)
1 to 2 tbsp coarse freshly cracked black pepper
1/2 cup water (for bottom of sheet pan during final sear)

ingredientGroups.title: Rosemary Salt (Full Batch)
items: Leaves stripped from 14 fresh rosemary sprigs
Leaves stripped from 8 fresh sage sprigs

ingredientGroups.title: Melted Onions
items: 2 large white or yellow onions, halved & thinly sliced root-to-tip
6 oz (1.5 sticks / 12 tbsp) unsalted butter, cold and cubed

ingredientGroups.title: Steakhouse Creme Fraiche Horseradish Sauce
items: 1/4 cup prepared horseradish, drained (1/3 cup for extra heat)
Kosher salt and black pepper to taste

ingredientGroups.title: Stovetop Rosemary-Garlic Au Jus
items: 1/2 cup dry red wine (Cabernet Sauvignon or Pinot Noir)
1 tbsp cold unsalted butter (whisked in right before serving)

steps.html: 1. Make the Rosemary Salt: Pulse 14 sprigs stripped rosemary, 8 sprigs stripped sage, 3-5 peeled garlic cloves, and the zest of 1 lemon in a food processor for 60 seconds until finely minced. Add 1 cup kosher salt and run another 30-45 seconds until it looks like bright-green damp sand.

2. Mix the Rub: Scoop 2.5 to 3 tbsp of the rosemary salt into a small bowl and stir in 1/2 tsp MSG (or 1 tbsp porcini powder). Spread leftover rosemary salt on a tray to air-dry overnight, then jar for future cooks.
3. Prep & Score: Pat the prime rib completely dry. Trim any hard fat cap down to ~1/2 inch thick and lightly score the fat in a shallow cross-hatch pattern without cutting into the meat.

4. Season & Dry Brine: Set the roast fat-side up on a wire rack over a rimmed baking sheet. Rub 3 tbsp Worcestershire sauce over every surface, then press the rosemary-umami salt evenly across all sides. Refrigerate uncovered for 24 to 48 hours.

instructionSections.title: 24 Hours Ahead: Horseradish Cream & Au Jus

steps.html: 1. Horseradish Sauce: Whisk mayonnaise, sour cream, creme fraiche, drained horseradish, lemon juice, Worcestershire sauce, and white wine vinegar until smooth. Fold in chopped chives, season with salt and black pepper, and refrigerate overnight so flavors meld.

2. Au Jus Base: Combine beef bone broth, dry red wine, soy sauce, Worcestershire sauce, rosemary sprigs, and smashed garlic in a saucepan over medium heat. Simmer 15-20 minutes until fragrant and slightly reduced. Strain and chill until dinner.

instructionSections.title: Day Of: Low-and-Slow Roast & Melted Onions

steps.html: 1. Temper & Pepper: Pull the roast 1 hour before cooking. Rub lightly with 2 tbsp neutral oil, coat generously with 1-2 tbsp coarse cracked black pepper, and insert a leave-in probe thermometer into the exact geometric center (avoiding bone).
2. Low Roast: Roast fat-side up at 200°F-225°F (standard bake, no convection) for roughly 3 to 4.5 hours depending on weight, until the center hits 115°F-118°F for edge-to-edge medium-rare.

3. Melted Onions: While the roast cooks, scrunch the thinly sliced onions and 2 tsp kosher salt in a heavy pot with clean hands for 1-2 minutes until juicy. Stew covered/uncovered over low heat for ~60 minutes, stirring every 5-10 minutes (adding a splash of water if dry) until completely soft. Over very low heat, stir in the 6 oz cold cubed butter a few cubes at a time so it emulsifies into a glossy, silky sauce.

1. Rest: Remove the roast at 115°F-118°F and rest 25-35 minutes (carryover brings it to 125°F-132°F). Travel option: vent uncovered 15 mins, wrap snugly in parchment then foil, and hold in a towel-packed insulated cooler up to 3 hours.

2. Blistering Sear: Crank oven to 475°F-500°F. Pat the roast exterior dry, pour 1/2 cup water into the bottom of the sheet pan beneath the wire rack to prevent smoke, and sear uncovered for 6-8 minutes until deeply browned and crisp.

3. Finish & Carve: Rewarm the au jus and whisk in 1 tbsp cold butter off the heat until glossy. Snip the twine, slice the rib eye off the bone in 1/2-inch slabs, and serve immediately with warm au jus, melted onions, and cold horseradish cream.

title: Nobu Miso Black Cod
description: Silky, buttery black cod marinated for 48 hours in sweet Saikyo miso and broiled on high until the edges blister into Nobu's signature mahogany caramelization.

ingredientGroups.title: Fish & Marinade
items: 4 black cod (sablefish) fillets, 6-8 oz each, skin-on and pin-bones removed
1/2 cup sweet white miso paste (Saikyo miso)
Pickled ginger shoots (hajikami) or pickled ginger, for plating

steps.html: 1. Make the Saikyo Miso Marinade: Combine sake and mirin in a small saucepan and bring to a boil for 20 seconds to cook off the alcohol. Turn heat to low, whisk in the white miso paste until dissolved, then whisk in the sugar until glossy and smooth. Cool completely to room temperature.
2. Marinate 48 Hours: Pat the black cod fillets thoroughly dry with paper towels, coat generously in the cooled miso marinade inside a glass dish or zip-top bag, and refrigerate for 48 hours.

3. Prep to Broil: Preheat the oven broiler to HIGH and line a rimmed sheet pan with foil. Gently wipe off excess marinade from each fillet with a paper towel, do not rinse, leaving a thin glaze on the fish.
4. Broil: Arrange fillets skin-side down on the foil-lined pan and broil on high for 8-12 minutes, watching closely after minute 6.
5. Check for Signature Char: Look for deep, dark golden-brown caramelization blistering along the edges while the center turns opaque and flakes effortlessly with a fork. Plate immediately.

title: Crispy Rice with Spicy Tuna
description: Nobu-style bite-sized blocks of chilled sushi rice deep-fried until shattering and golden, crowned with finely diced sashimi-grade ahi tuna in Kewpie-sriracha dressing.

ingredientGroups.title: Crispy Sushi Rice
items: 2 cups cooked seasoned short-grain sushi rice, pressed firmly into a pan & chilled overnight

ingredientGroups.title: Spicy Tuna Mixture
items: 1/2 lb sushi-grade ahi tuna, very finely diced
Optional garnish: paper-thin jalapeño or sliced green onion

steps.html: 1. Press Rice Overnight: Pack warm seasoned sushi rice firmly into a plastic-lined rectangular pan (~3/4-inch thick), cover, and chill overnight until completely firm.

2. Mix the Spicy Tuna: With a sharp knife on a cold cutting board, dice the sushi-grade ahi tuna very finely, uniform tiny cubes with texture, not a paste. Gently fold in Kewpie mayonnaise, sriracha, sesame oil, and soy sauce. Cover and keep chilled.

3. Cut & Fry Crispy Rice: Slice the cold rice block into bite-sized rectangles using a wet sharp knife so it doesn't stick. Heat oil to 350°F and deep-fry in batches for 2-3 minutes until crisp and golden brown on all sides.
4. Drain & Top: Drain crispy rice on a wire rack (holds crisp for 30-45 minutes), then spoon a generous mound of chilled spicy tuna onto each warm cake right before serving.

title: Yellowtail Sashimi with Jalapeño
description: Chilled ribbons of sushi-grade hamachi brushed with a whisper of garlic purée, topped with paper-thin jalapeño and fresh cilantro in a bright 2:1 yuzu-soy dressing.

ingredientGroups.title: Sashimi & Garnish
items: 1 small clove fresh garlic, puréed into a smooth paste
Fresh cilantro leaves (1 tender leaf per slice)

steps.html: 1. Make Yuzu Soy: Whisk together the 60 ml yuzu juice and 30 ml soy sauce in a small jar and chill thoroughly.

2. Slice & Garlic-Kiss the Hamachi: Working on a cold board, slice the yellowtail cleanly. Lightly touch the underside of each slice with a tiny, barely visible dot of garlic purée, just enough for aroma.

3. Garnish & Chill: Arrange slices flat on a chilled plate and top each piece with one paper-thin jalapeño ring and a single cilantro leaf. Cover tightly with plastic wrap and keep refrigerated until service.
4. Dress at the Last Second: Right before serving, drizzle the cold yuzu soy lightly over the fish so it glazes without curing the sashimi, and serve immediately.

title: Oysters with Ponzu Mignonette
description: Ice-cold freshly shucked oysters dressed with a bright Japanese mignonette of rice wine vinegar, soy sauce, lemon, toasted sesame oil, shallot, and green onion.

ingredientGroups.title: Oysters & Ponzu Mignonette
items: 2 tsp shallot, very finely minced (~1/3 small shallot)
1 tbsp green onion (green parts only), thinly sliced

steps.html: 1. Make the Mignonette First: Whisk the rice wine vinegar, soy sauce, fresh lemon juice, sugar, and sesame oil until the sugar completely dissolves.
2. Mellow the Aromatics: Stir in the finely minced shallot and sliced green onion. Refrigerate at least 20-30 minutes (or several hours ahead) so the shallots mellow in the citrus-soy liquid.
3. Shuck & Serve: Shuck the oysters clean of any shell grit, nestle level on a platter of crushed ice or rock salt, and spoon ~1/2 teaspoon of chilled ponzu mignonette over each oyster.

title: Biang Biang Braised Pork Noodles
description: Interactive dinner-party hand-pulled wide belt noodles topped with 3.5-hour star-anise braised pork, sizzling 350°F garlic-chili oil, spicy cucumber salad, and blistered shishitos.

ingredientGroups.title: Triple Hand-Pulled Noodle Dough (38-40 Pieces)
items: Neutral oil (for heavily coating every dough rectangle)

ingredientGroups.title: Bowl Base, Hot-Oil Sizzle & Greens
items: Per bowl base: 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp Chinese black vinegar, pinch sugar, pinch MSG
6 scallions, thinly sliced & 2 fresh chillies, sliced
Coarse Sichuan chili flakes, Doubanjiang & toasted sesame seeds
1 cup lard or neutral cooking oil (heated to 350°F)
14 oz fresh spinach + 6 garlic cloves cut into slivers

ingredientGroups.title: Spicy Cucumber Salad & Garlic Shishitos
items: 12 cucumbers, spiralized + 4 tsp salt (for salting & rinsing)
Cucumber dressing: 2 tbsp soy sauce, 4 minced garlic cloves, 2 tbsp rice vinegar, 2 tbsp chili oil, 2 tbsp sugar, 2 tsp sesame oil, 2 tsp sesame seeds
10 garlic cloves sliced into thin chips, 2.5 tsp sesame oil & 2.5 tsp soy sauce

instructionSections.title: Braised Pork & Resting the Belt-Noodle Dough

steps.html: 1. Prep Aromatics: Mince 30 garlic cloves for the noodle station, slice 10 cloves into thin chips for shishitos, and sliver 6 cloves for spinach. Slice chillies and scallions.

2. Oven-Braise the Pork (3.5 Hours): Combine pork stock, Shaoxing wine, soy sauce, star anise, ginger, bruised garlic, pork belly chunks, and pork shoulder in a heavy Dutch oven. Cover and braise in a 300°F (150°C) oven for 3.5 hours until fork-tender, then shred and moisten with braising jus.
3. Mix & Knead Noodle Dough: Mix 1.4 kg flour, 20g kosher salt, and 700g water into a shaggy dough. Wrap in plastic and rest 20 minutes, then knead 5 minutes until smooth.

4. Portion & Oil Heavily: Roll dough into logs and cut into 38-40 pieces (~50g each). Flatten each into a 5-6 inch rectangle, coat every surface generously in oil so they never skin over, layer on a tray, wrap tightly in plastic, and rest at room temperature (at least 1-2 hours for effortless stretching).

instructionSections.title: Sides & The Interactive Hot-Oil Noodle Sizzle

steps.html: 1. Chilled Spicy Cucumbers: Toss spiralized cucumbers with 4 tsp salt, sit 5 minutes, rinse 3 times, and drain well. Toss with soy sauce, minced garlic, rice vinegar, chili oil, sugar, sesame oil, and sesame seeds; chill immediately.

2. Spinach & Blistered Shishitos: Sauté the 6 slivered garlic cloves with 14 oz spinach and set aside. Blister shishitos in a smoking-hot wok with oil and salt; crisp the 10 garlic chips, then toss peppers back in with 2.5 tsp sesame oil and 2.5 tsp soy sauce.

3. Set the Bowl Station: Line up 12 bowls, each dosed with 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp black vinegar, a pinch of sugar, and a pinch of MSG. Set out bowls of chili flakes, Doubanjiang, minced garlic, scallions, and sesame seeds.

4. Pull, Boil & Sizzle: Bring two large pots of water to a rolling boil and heat 1 cup lard or neutral oil to 350°F. Indent each oiled dough rectangle lengthwise with a chopstick, stretch and slap against the counter into long wide ribbons, tear down the center seam, and boil 90 seconds.

5. The Finish: Pile hot noodles into the seasoned bowls, top with shredded braised pork, spinach, scallions, garlic, and chili flakes, then ladle smoking 350°F oil directly over the aromatics so they sizzle and bloom. Toss immediately!

title: Chicken Panang Curry
description: Velvety Thai red coconut curry enriched with creamy peanut butter, tender sliced chicken, sweet bell peppers, fresh ginger, lime juice, and fragrant basil over hot jasmine rice.

ingredientGroups.title: Panang Curry
items: 4 lbs chicken breasts, sliced thin against the grain
2 cups loosely packed fresh basil leaves, roughly chopped
Hot cooked jasmine, white, or brown rice, for serving

steps.html: 1. Heat oil over medium-high heat in a large skillet or Dutch oven. Sauté sliced onions for 2 minutes, then add bell peppers, minced garlic, and grated ginger and sauté 2 minutes more until fragrant.

2. Stir in the Panang curry paste and peanut butter and fry for 1 minute to bloom the spices. Pour in most of the coconut milk, whisk the cornstarch smoothly into the remaining 1/2 can of coconut milk, and stir it into the pot.
3. Add the sliced chicken, stirring to coat. Simmer gently for 10-15 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the coconut-peanut sauce thickens.
4. Stir in brown sugar, fish sauce, fresh lime juice, and chopped basil. Simmer 5 minutes more and adjust salt and pepper to taste.
5. Ladle generously over steaming hot jasmine rice.

title: Beef Pad See Ew
description: Wok-charred wide rice noodles tossed with soy-marinated flank steak, crisp-tender Chinese broccoli, scrambled eggs, and a caramelized dark soy and oyster sauce glaze.

ingredientGroups.title: Steak, Noodles & Greens
items: 3 lbs flank steak, sliced thin against the grain
3 lbs fresh wide rice noodles, cut into 1/2-inch ribbons (or dried wide rice noodles)
18 stalks Chinese broccoli (gai lan), cut into 2-inch pieces
Thinly sliced scallions & toasted sesame seeds, for garnish

ingredientGroups.title: Marinade & Stir-Fry Glaze
items: 6 tbsp light soy sauce (divided between beef marinade and stir-fry sauce)
Fish sauce & kosher salt, to taste

steps.html: 1. Toss the thinly sliced flank steak with light soy sauce in a bowl and marinate while prepping the remaining ingredients.
2. Boil or soak the wide rice noodles just until tender-pliable (2-3 minutes for fresh), drain thoroughly, and toss with a drizzle of oil so they don't stick together.
3. Whisk together the dark soy sauce, remaining light soy sauce, minced garlic, oyster sauce, rice vinegar, brown sugar, and MSG until the sugar dissolves.

4. Heat oil in a smoking-hot wok over medium-high to high heat. Sear the beef in batches for 2-3 minutes until browned, toss in the Chinese broccoli for 2 minutes until crisp-tender, and transfer to a bowl.

5. Add remaining oil to the wok, crack in the eggs, and scramble for ~1 minute. Add the noodles and sauce, folding gently so the dark soy caramelizes onto the wide noodles, then return the steak and Chinese broccoli for 2 minutes with a dash of fish sauce.
6. Plate hot and finish with thinly sliced scallions and toasted sesame seeds.

title: Artisan Dutch Oven Bread
description: Crackling golden crust and airy, open-crumb artisan boule made with four pantry staples, gentle stretch-and-folds, and steam-baked inside a blazing-hot Dutch oven.

ingredientGroups.title: Dough (5 Hours Total)
items: 600g all-purpose flour (about 4 cups, lightly packed and leveled)
1 envelope instant or active dry yeast (7g)

steps.html: Video reference: Artisan Dutch Oven Bread Walkthrough
1. Instant yeast does NOT need to be bloomed first, mix flour, yeast, and salt directly in a large bowl by hand, make a well in the center, and pour in the lukewarm water.

2. Wet your working hand so dough doesn't stick and mix until a rough dough pulls away from the sides of the bowl (adjust by 1 tbsp flour if too sticky or 1 tbsp water if dry). Cover and let rise until doubled in size (1.5 to 2 hours).
3. Uncover and poke gently with a wet finger, properly risen dough indents and slowly deflates.
4. Working around the bowl in 90° turns, pull dough loose from the sides and fold up toward the center until taut. Cover and rise again for 1.5 to 2 hours.
5. Turn out onto a lightly floured counter, fold underneath several times into a tight round boule, pinch seams underneath, and place seam-side down in an oiled, floured bowl. Cover and proof 1 hour.
6. Place an empty 6-quart Dutch oven (with lid) inside the oven and preheat to 450°F (230°C) for 45 minutes.
7. Carefully turn the proofed boule into the screaming-hot pot, cover with the lid, and bake at 450°F for 30 minutes, then remove the lid and bake 15 minutes more until deep chestnut brown.
8. Cool on a wire rack for at least 10-20 minutes before slicing.

title: Signature Chicken Marinades (7 Flavors)
description: Seven high-flavor bulk meal-prep marinades, each scaled consistently for 10 lbs of boneless, skinless chicken breast: Korean Gochujang, Yakitori, Teriyaki, Cantonese Char Siu, Vietnamese Lemongrass, Peruvian Pollo a la Brasa, and Fiery Harissa.

ingredientGroups.title: 1. Gochujang Chicken (6-8 Hrs Max · 10 lbs Chicken Breast)
items: 10 lbs boneless skinless chicken breast, butterflied or pounded even
1/2 cup low-sodium soy sauce & 1/4 cup toasted sesame oil
1/4 cup (4 tbsp) each garlic powder, onion powder & paprika
1 tsp kosher salt & 1 tsp black pepper

ingredientGroups.title: 2. Yakitori Marinade (12 Hrs · 10 lbs Chicken Breast)
items: 10 lbs boneless skinless chicken breast, butterflied or cubed for skewers

ingredientGroups.title: 3. Teriyaki Marinade (12 Hrs · 10 lbs Chicken Breast)
items: 10 lbs boneless skinless chicken breast, butterflied or pounded even
6 tbsp unseasoned rice wine vinegar & 6 tbsp toasted sesame oil

ingredientGroups.title: 4. Macro Cantonese Char Siu (12-24 Hrs · 10 lbs Chicken Breast)
items: 10 lbs boneless skinless chicken breast, butterflied or pounded even
1/3 cup regular soy sauce & 1/4 cup dark soy sauce
1/3 cup Shaoxing wine & 2 tbsp toasted sesame oil
3 cubes red fermented bean curd (nam yue), mashed with 2 tbsp jar liquid
12 cloves garlic (microplaned) + 2 tbsp garlic powder + 1 tbsp onion powder
1.5 tbsp Chinese five-spice & 1.5 tsp white pepper
1 tsp xanthan gum (whisked in last so marinade clings like a glaze)

ingredientGroups.title: 5. Vietnamese Lemongrass & Garlic (12-24 Hrs · 10 lbs Chicken Breast)
items: 10 lbs boneless skinless chicken breast, butterflied or pounded even
1/3 cup regular soy sauce & 1/3 cup fish sauce (Red Boat)
1/4 cup avocado/neutral oil & 3 tbsp unseasoned rice vinegar
4 large shallots (grated into paste) & 12 cloves garlic (microplaned)
1.5 tbsp cracked black pepper, 1 tbsp red pepper flakes (or 6 Thai chilies) & 1 tbsp ground coriander

ingredientGroups.title: 6. Peruvian Pollo a la Brasa (12-24 Hrs · 10 lbs Chicken Breast)
items: 10 lbs boneless skinless chicken breast, butterflied or pounded even
1/2 cup regular soy sauce & 1/4 cup Dijon mustard
3 tbsp red wine vinegar, 3 tbsp Golden Monkfruit & 3 tbsp avocado oil
3.5 tbsp toasted ground cumin & 2.5 tbsp smoked paprika
1.5 tbsp crushed Mexican oregano, 1 tbsp black pepper & 1.5 tsp kosher salt

ingredientGroups.title: 7. Fiery Harissa & Toasted Spice (8-24 Hrs · 10 lbs Chicken Breast)
items: 10 lbs boneless skinless chicken breast, butterflied or pounded even
3/4 cup spicy Harissa paste (zero added sugar, e.g., Mina or DEA)
1/3 cup regular soy sauce & 1/3 cup tomato paste
1/3 cup Golden Monkfruit, 1/4 cup red wine vinegar & 1/3 cup olive oil
3 tbsp cumin, 2 tbsp coriander, 2 tbsp smoked paprika & 1 tbsp onion powder
1.5 tsp ground cinnamon & 1.5 tsp kosher salt

instructionSections.title: Marinating & High-Heat Char (Scaled for 10 lbs Chicken Breast)

steps.html: 1. Prep the Chicken: Every marinade above is scaled for 10 lbs of boneless, skinless chicken breast (tap 0.5x above for a 5-lb batch). Butterfly or pound thick breasts to an even thickness so they absorb flavor and cook evenly.

2. Whisk Smooth: Whisk all ingredients for your chosen marinade in a large bowl until fully emulsified (if making Cantonese Char Siu, whisk the xanthan gum in last so it thickens into a clingy glaze without clumping).

3. Cure & Marinate: Toss the 10 lbs of chicken breast in heavy-duty zip-top bags or Cambro containers, massaging to coat every surface. Respect the window: 6-8 hours max for Gochujang so it stays tender, 12 hours for Yakitori and Teriyaki, and 12-24 hours for Char Siu, Lemongrass, Pollo a la Brasa, and Harissa.

4. Grill, Broil, or Air-Fry: Cook over a medium-high oiled grill, under the oven broiler, or in a 400°F air fryer, flipping until edges blister and caramelize and internal temperature hits 160°F-165°F. Rest 5-10 minutes before slicing against the grain.

title: Honey Balsamic Vinaigrette
description: Glossy five-ingredient house vinaigrette balancing aged balsamic vinegar, floral honey, smooth Dijon mustard, and extra-virgin olive oil.

ingredientGroups.title: Vinaigrette
items: Coarse kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

steps.html: 1. Whisk the balsamic vinegar, honey, and Dijon mustard in a small bowl (or add to a mason jar) until smooth.
2. Slowly stream in the extra-virgin olive oil while whisking vigorously, or seal the mason jar and shake hard for 15 seconds, until thick and glossy.
3. Season generously with coarse salt and freshly cracked black pepper to taste. Keeps refrigerated in a sealed jar for up to 2 weeks.

title: Homemade Honey Mustard
description: Punchy, textured stone-ground and Dijon honey mustard brightened with fresh lemon juice, minced garlic, and cold-pressed olive oil.

ingredientGroups.title: Dressing & Dip
items: 1/4 cup extra-virgin or cold-pressed olive oil

steps.html: 1. Combine fresh lemon juice, honey, stone-ground mustard, Dijon mustard, minced garlic, salt, and black pepper in a bowl or mason jar.
2. Whisk while streaming in the extra-virgin olive oil (or shake tightly in a jar) until creamy and emulsified.
3. Taste and adjust honey or lemon juice as desired; chill 15 minutes before drizzling over greens, grain bowls, or crispy chicken.

title: Ninja Creami Oreo McFlurry
description: Ultra-thick vanilla bean high-protein soft-serve spun in the Ninja Creami with chunky Oreo Thins folded throughout, 281 calories and 23g protein for the entire pint.

ingredientGroups.title: Ice Cream Base (281 cal · 31g C · 6g F · 23g P)
items: 5g (1 tsp) vanilla bean paste (or vanilla extract)

steps.html: 1. Blend all base ingredients until completely smooth, pour into a Ninja Creami pint, and freeze flat for at least 16 hours.
2. Run the outside of the frozen pint under hot water for 60 seconds.
3. Spin on the Lite Ice Cream setting, then run a Respin cycle (respin once more if still slightly powdery).
4. Carve a tunnel down the center of the pint with a butter knife, pack in the 3 Oreo Thins, and run the Mix-In cycle.

title: Ninja Creami Thai Tea Ice Cream
description: Fragrant brewed Thai iced tea spun into silky, macro-friendly ice cream and finished with a ribbon of sweetened condensed milk, 172 calories and 18g protein per pint.

ingredientGroups.title: Thai Tea Base (172 cal · 19g C · 2g F · 18g P)

steps.html: 1. Blend all base ingredients until smooth and freeze level in a Ninja Creami pint for at least 16 hours.
2. Run the pint exterior under hot water for at least 60 seconds.
3. Spin on Lite Ice Cream, followed by Respin (and one extra Respin if powdery).
4. Drizzle the 15g sweetened condensed milk over the top and enjoy immediately.

title: Ninja Creami Double Oreo
description: Midnight-dark black cocoa chocolate protein ice cream tasting just like an Oreo wafer, packed with mixed-in and crumbled Oreos, 299 calories and 35g protein per pint.

ingredientGroups.title: Black Cocoa Base (299 cal · 28g C · 9g F · 35g P)

steps.html: 1. Blend the chocolate protein shake, sweetener, black cocoa powder, salt, and xanthan gum until jet-black and lump-free; freeze in a Creami pint at least 16 hours.
2. Run under hot water for 60 seconds, spin on Lite Ice Cream, and Respin until fudgy and smooth.
3. Hollow a center well with a butter knife, drop in 3/4 of the Oreos, and run the Mix-In cycle.
4. Crumble the remaining Oreos right on top before serving.

title: Ninja Creami Cookie Dough
description: Rich vanilla bean protein ice cream loaded with real Ben & Jerry's chocolate chip cookie dough bites, 350 calories and a massive 43g protein per pint.

ingredientGroups.title: Vanilla Bean Base (350 cal · 27g C · 8g F · 43g P)
items: 1 Vanilla Protein Shake (Fairlife Core Power Elite, 230 cal, 42g protein)

ingredientGroups.title: Mix-Ins
items: 28g (1 serving) pre-made edible cookie dough bites (Ben & Jerry's Cookie Dough Pieces)

steps.html: 1. Blend all base ingredients smoothly and freeze flat for at least 16 hours.
2. Run the frozen pint under hot water for 60 seconds, spin on Lite Ice Cream, and run Respin until dense and creamy.
3. Carve a hole down to the bottom with a butter knife, fill with the chilled cookie dough pieces, and run the Mix-In cycle.

title: Ninja Creami Shamrock Shake
description: Cool mint and vanilla bean frozen protein soft-serve that nails the classic seasonal Shamrock Shake at just 150 calories, 2g carbs, and 30g protein.

ingredientGroups.title: Shamrock Base (150 cal · 2g C · 3g F · 30g P)

steps.html: 1. Blend all ingredients until smooth and pastel mint-green, then freeze flat in a Ninja Creami pint for at least 16 hours.
2. Rinse the outside of the pint under hot water for 60 seconds.
3. Spin on Lite Ice Cream, then run Respin once or twice until silky soft-serve consistency.

title: Yuzu Blackberry Caipiroska
description: Nobu-inspired cocktail of muddled ripe blackberries, floral Japanese yuzu juice, simple syrup, and chilled vodka poured unstrained over crushed rocks with mint and dried citrus.

steps.html: 1. Muddle: In a cocktail shaker, muddle the fresh blackberries with simple syrup until completely broken down and juicy.
2. Shake Hard: Add the vodka and yuzu juice, fill with ice, and shake hard for 10-15 seconds.

3. Dirty Dump & Garnish: Pour the entire contents, ice, crushed berry pulp, and all, straight into a rocks glass. Slap the mint sprig between your palms to release its oils and garnish alongside a dried citrus wheel.

title: "Winter Green" Cucumber, Mint & Lime Cooler
description: Vibrant emerald-green party pitcher cocktail blending peel-on English cucumbers, fresh mint, razor-sharp lime juice, vodka, and an optional subtle jalapeño kick.

ingredientGroups.title: Batched Dispenser / Pitcher
items: 2 large English cucumbers, chopped with peel on (for emerald color)
0.5 to 0.75 cup simple syrup (to balance the lime)
2.5 cups cold water (or omit and let guests top with club soda)
Optional: 1/2 seeded jalapeño for a subtle warming kick

steps.html: 1. Blend the chopped peel-on cucumbers, fresh mint leaves, lime juice, simple syrup, and optional seeded jalapeño on high for 20 seconds until completely liquefied.
2. Pour through a fine-mesh strainer into a large pitcher or drink dispenser, pressing the solids firmly to extract every drop of bright emerald juice.
3. Stir in the 750 ml vodka and cold water (or serve concentrated over ice topped with club soda) and chill thoroughly before guests arrive.

title: Blackberry Sage Blanco Batch
description: Crowd-pleasing 20-drink blanco tequila pitcher infused with blended fresh blackberries, 25 aromatic sage leaves, fresh lime juice, and agave.

ingredientGroups.title: 20-Drink Party Batch
items: 5 cups fresh blackberries (~26 oz), plus whole berries for picks
2 cups agave nectar & simple syrup blend
25 fresh sage leaves (plus extra whole leaves for garnish)

steps.html: 1. Blend the Base: Combine the 5 cups blackberries, fresh lime juice, agave/simple syrup sweetener, and all 25 sage leaves in a blender and blend on high until liquefied.
2. Fine-Strain: Pour through a fine-mesh strainer directly into a large pitcher, pressing with a spoon to extract all ruby juice while catching seeds and herb bits.
3. Batch & Chill: Stir in the 5 cups blanco tequila, cover tightly, and refrigerate for a few hours so the earthy sage and berry flavors marry.
4. Serve: Stir vigorously right before pouring over fresh rocks. Garnish each glass with two skewered blackberries and a single fresh sage leaf resting on the ice.
